newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: United's Dunne extends lead in Ohariu.
newsitem.headline: United's Dunne extends lead in Ohariu.

text.p: An opinion poll in the Wellington seat of Ohariu-Belmont has confirmed the National Party's current coalition partner United should make it back into Parliament.
United's Peter Dunne regustered 54 percent support in a poll taken for Wellington's Evening Post newspaper, up from 45 percent in a similar poll in July.
The ruling National Party has opted not to stand a candidate against Dunne in the seat.

United has seven MPs in parliament but polling ahead of the October 12 election has its support hovering around one percent nationally -- scarcely enough to qualify it for a second MP under the proportional representation system adopted for this election.
Among the opposition parties Labour's Verna Smith registered 15 percent support, down from 25 in July, against 21 percent for Phillida Bunkle of the left-wing Alliance, up from 13 percent.
New Zealand First's Ernie Davis, a late replacement for dumped candidate Rex Widerstrom, gained three percent and the morals-based Christian Coalition candidate Romemarie Thomas one percent.
Former Labour Party cabinet minister and free-market ACT New Zealand candidate Ken Shirley scored three percent support.

In the party vote, which determines the overall percentage of seats a party gets in parliament, National was on 50 percent in Ohariu-Belmont, up three on the July poll. Labour was down seven at 17 percent and the Alliance up four at 13 percent. New Zealand First was down one at eight, and ACT and the Christian
Coalition were each up one at four percent.
On the party vote Dunne's United scored only one percent.
Of the 300 voters polled, 14 percent were undecided.
